name: Hugging Face
summary: Hugging Face is a New York-based company that runs the Hugging Face Hub, a platform for sharing AI models, datasets and demo apps. Its own teams also release [open models](https://huggingface.co/blog/smollm), such as the SmolLM small language models.

incidents.title: Hugging Face Detects Unauthorized Access to Spaces Secrets
incidents.summary: Hugging Face said it detected unauthorized access to its Spaces platform and suspected that some Spaces secrets were accessed without permission. It revoked the affected tokens.
incidents.description: In May 2024, [Hugging Face said](https://huggingface.co/blog/space-secrets-disclosure) that it found unauthorized access to its Spaces platform. It suspected that some secrets, such as API keys and tokens that users stored, were accessed without permission. The company revoked the affected tokens, told affected users, and [did not say](https://techcrunch.com/2024/05/31/hugging-face-says-it-detected-unauthorized-access-to-its-ai-model-hosting-platform/) how many users were affected.

timeline.title: Unauthorized access detected
timeline.description: Hugging Face detects unauthorized access to Spaces in the last week of May 2024.

timeline.title: Public disclosure
timeline.description: Hugging Face publishes a disclosure, revokes tokens and advises users to refresh their keys.

timeline.title: Further press coverage
timeline.description: CSO Online reports on the breach and notes that its scale was not disclosed.

incidents.title: Wiz Researchers Found Cross-Tenant Access Flaws in Hugging Face Infrastructure
incidents.summary: Hugging Face said that Wiz researchers found shortcomings in its sandboxed compute environments by running arbitrary code through a pickle-format model ([Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/blog/hugging-face-wiz-security-blog)). Hugging Face said it resolved all issues related to the exploit.
incidents.description: [Wiz researchers said](https://www.wiz.io/blog/wiz-and-hugging-face-address-risks-to-ai-infrastructure) that they uploaded a malicious pickle model to the Hugging Face Inference API and used it to get access to the models of other customers. They also said that they could overwrite container images that other Spaces customers used. [Hugging Face said](https://huggingface.co/blog/hugging-face-wiz-security-blog) that it resolved all the issues.

timeline.title: Hugging Face discloses the findings
timeline.description: Hugging Face publishes a post on the Wiz findings and says it resolved the issues.

timeline.title: Wiz publishes its research
timeline.description: Wiz describes cross-tenant access through the Inference API and write access to a shared container registry.

timeline.title: Press coverage
timeline.description: Dark Reading reports on the two flaws and Hugging Face's mitigations.

incidents.title: Fake Qwen2 Models on Hugging Face Installed Cryptominers and Backdoors, Researchers Say
incidents.summary: [Pluto Security reported](https://pluto.security/blog/hugging-face-malware-campaign-load-mine/) that 31 repositories on the Hugging Face Hub posed as small Qwen2 test models and ran a hidden cryptominer, and in some builds a backdoor, on machines that loaded them with `trust_remote_code`. [BleepingComputer reported](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/hugging-face-malware-campaign-returns-to-hijack-gpus-for-crypto-mining/) that a second wave came back within days of the first takedown and that its top repository had more than 28,000 downloads.
incidents.description: [Pluto Security said](https://pluto.security/blog/hugging-face-malware-campaign-load-mine/) that 31 Hugging Face repositories posed as small Qwen2 test models and ran a hidden cryptominer, and sometimes a backdoor, on machines that loaded them with remote code. A second wave reportedly came back within days of the first takedown. [BleepingComputer reported](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/hugging-face-malware-campaign-returns-to-hijack-gpus-for-crypto-mining/) that Hugging Face disabled the top repository, but a near-identical copy is still live.

timeline.title: Pluto Security publishes the campaign
timeline.description: Pluto Security names the campaign Load/Mine and says the repositories and linked models have more than 32,000 downloads ([Pluto Security](https://pluto.security/blog/hugging-face-malware-campaign-load-mine/)).

timeline.title: Top repository disabled, a copy stays live
timeline.description: [BleepingComputer reports](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/hugging-face-malware-campaign-returns-to-hijack-gpus-for-crypto-mining/) that Hugging Face disabled the most downloaded repository, but a near-identical copy uploaded on October 25 is still live.
